newsitem.title: USA: Boeing appoints chief for Douglas operations.
newsitem.headline: Boeing appoints chief for Douglas operations.

text.p: Boeing Co. Friday appointed long-time executive Richard Pearson to head the commercial aircraft operations acquired in its purchase of McDonnell Douglas Corp.
Pearson, who joined Boeing in 1967, led the company's commercial airplane group transition team in the seven months leading up to the $16.3 billion merger, which became effective Friday.

Pearson eventually will move to California to oversee the Douglas Products Division, formerly known as Douglas Aircraft Co., which makes the MD-80, MD-90, MD-95 and MD-11 airplanes at plants in Orange County.

The long-term fate of those models is uncertain, although Boeing Chairman Phil Condit said last week he saw potential for derivatives of the new MD-95 that would be smaller than any plane the company currently offers.
Walter Orlowski, who had served as president of Douglas Aircraft, will move to Seattle to become a vice president in Boaing's commercial airplane group.
Boeing has not yet made any announcements about management of its defense and space operations, which constitute the bulk of the assets acquired in the merger.

A company spokesman said "no consensus" was reached on whether the operations will be based in Seattle or St. Louis, where fighter jets including the F-15 and F/A 18 are manufactured. A reorganization also is possible.

Alan Mulally, the recently appointed president of Boeing's defense and space operations, is on vacation and will not take part in any of the "Day One" celebrations planned for Monday at 40 Boeing sites across the country, a spokesman said.
